sentences.zh: 它还是像你自己带

sentences.en: NGINX, or is it built into Kubernetes?
sentences.zh: NGINX 那样，还是内置在 Kubernetes 里的？

sentences.en: How does that work?
sentences.zh: 这到底是怎么运作的？

sentences.en: Yeah, so generally, nowadays, you know, you'll have services, managed Kubernetes services, you don't have to roll the whole thing and manage it yourself.
sentences.zh: 对，通常来说，现在，你知道的，你会有服务，托管的 Kubernetes 服务，你不必自己从头搭建和管理整个系统。

sentences.en: So you'll have things like EKS and on AWS,
sentences.zh: 所以你会拥有诸如 AWS 上的 EKS，

sentences.en: AKS on Azure, GKE on Google Cloud Engine, and you're able to just using those actually have access to the native load balancers within those cloud vendors.
sentences.zh: Azure 上的 AKS，Google Cloud Engine 上的 GKE，你能够直接使用这些服务来访问这些云厂商内部的原生负载均衡器。

sentences.en: So you don't have to go and roll your own
sentences.zh: 所以你不必去自己搞一个

sentences.en: NGINX load balancer container and spin it up and manage it.
sentences.zh: NGINX 负载均衡器容器，然后把它启动并进行管理。

sentences.en: You can just say, look, give me the, you know, Azure load balancer, the Google load balancer, the AWS load balancer for this set of resources.
sentences.zh: 你只需说，听着，为这组资源给我提供，你知道的，Azure 负载均衡器、谷歌负载均衡器、AWS 负载均衡器。

sentences.en: So that's generally nowadays, given the maturity and all the managed service in the space, how folks will leverage those things.
sentences.zh: 所以现在通常情况下，鉴于该领域的成熟度和各种托管服务，大家都会这样来利用这些东西。

sentences.en: It's completely abstracted away, as it should be, in my opinion.
sentences.zh: 它被完全抽象化了，依我来看，理当如此。

sentences.en: But fundamentally, it's not doing anything different, right?
sentences.zh: 但从根本上说，它并没有做任何不同的事情，对吧？

sentences.en: It's saying, hey, as I get more volume, and it's more robust, obviously, than rolling it yourself, because
sentences.zh: 它是在说，嘿，随着我的数据量增加，而且它显然比你自己搭建要更加稳健，因为

sentences.en: this is our, you know, big managed services from these massive hyperscale cloud providers that manage, you know, traffic for Netflix and things like that.
sentences.zh: 这是我们，你知道的，来自那些为 Netflix 等公司管理流量的庞大超大规模云提供商的大型托管服务。

sentences.en: So they really scale up.
sentences.zh: 所以它们的规模真的很大。

sentences.en: But fundamentally, it's the same thing.
sentences.zh: 但从根本上说，是一样的东西。

sentences.en: As I get more volume, you know, I'll report out on the volume I'm getting.
sentences.zh: 随着我的数据量增加，你知道的，我会报告我收到的数据量。

sentences.en: So you can use that for intelligent decisions downstream.
sentences.zh: 这样你就可以将其用于下游的智能决策。

sentences.en: And I will segment that volume in a way that is not necessarily overloading any given resource within the cluster.
sentences.zh: 我会对这些数据量进行分段，以确保不会使集群中的任何给定资源过载。

sentences.en: Got it.
sentences.zh: 明白了。

sentences.en: Okay, that makes sense.
sentences.zh: 好的，这讲得通。

sentences.en: So I see.
sentences.zh: 我明白了。

sentences.en: So the individual nodes have some way of telling the load balancer, you know, I'm in trouble, or, you know, I have a ton of work, or I'm available.
sentences.zh: 所以各个节点有一种方法可以告诉负载均衡器，你知道的，我遇到麻烦了，或者，你知道的，我有大量的工作，或者我很空闲。

sentences.en: And then the load balancer then can, you know, send things to the right.
sentences.zh: 然后负载均衡器就可以，你知道的，把事情发送到正确的地方。

sentences.en: So a pod is a group of machines, and the load balancer is always sending it to the same pod, but just to a different machine in the pod.
sentences.zh: 所以 Pod 是一组机器，负载均衡器总是把它发送到同一个 Pod，但只是发送到 Pod 中的不同机器上？

sentences.en: Is that how it works?
sentences.zh: 是这样运作的吗？

sentences.en: So it depends, right?
sentences.zh: 这得看情况，对吧？

sentences.en: Generally, a pod is a group of containers, not machines, the machines are the actual nodes.
sentences.zh: 通常，Pod 是一组容器，而不是机器，机器才是实际的节点。

sentences.en: So you can have multiple pods running on a machine with multiple containers within them.
sentences.zh: 所以你可以在一台机器上运行多个 Pod，其中包含多个容器。

sentences.en: And the load balancer can be configured in different ways.
sentences.zh: 并且负载均衡器可以通过不同的方式进行配置。

sentences.en: But generally, it could send it to, you know, multiple pods, or a single pod that's scaling up or scaling down, there's kind of nuance in how you configure it.
sentences.zh: 但通常，它可以将其发送到，你知道的，多个 Pod，或者一个正在扩容或缩容的单个 Pod，这取决于你如何配置它，其中有一些细微差别。

sentences.en: It's kind of an open playground.
sentences.zh: 这有点像一个开放的游乐场。

sentences.en: But I think the most common thing is you'll have, you know, something like a vertical pod autoscaler,
sentences.zh: 但我认为最常见的情况是，你会拥有，你知道的，类似于垂直 Pod 自动扩缩容工具的东西，

sentences.en: and the load balancer would be sending to maybe, you know, two different pods, or one pod that's scaling up, scaling down.
sentences.zh: 并且负载均衡器会发送到，也许，你知道的，两个不同的 Pod，或者一个正在扩容、缩容的 Pod。

sentences.en: Got it.
sentences.zh: 明白了。

sentences.en: Okay, so this is a good time to transition to that.
sentences.zh: 好的，现在是过渡到那个话题的好时机。

sentences.en: So what is autoscaling?
sentences.zh: 那么什么是自动扩缩容？

sentences.en: And what is horizontal and vertical autoscaling?
sentences.zh: 什么是水平自动扩缩容和垂直自动扩缩容？

sentences.en: What does that distinction mean?
sentences.zh: 这种区别意味着什么？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So horizontal autoscaling and vertical autoscaling, I think, are pretty simple concepts when you think about it outside of like all this mess of containers and namespaces.
sentences.zh: 所以水平自动扩缩容和垂直自动扩缩容，我认为当你不去考虑所有这些混乱的容器和命名空间时，是相当简单的概念。

sentences.en: You know, horizontal just means add more computers.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，水平扩缩容只意味着添加更多计算机。

sentences.en: And vertical just means make the computer bigger.
sentences.zh: 而垂直扩缩容只意味着把计算机做大。

sentences.en: It's kind of the way I think about it.
sentences.zh: 这就是我对它的理解方式。

sentences.en: And those things are the same, whether you're managing VMs or containers or whatever.
sentences.zh: 无论你管理的是虚拟机、容器还是别的什么，这些东西都是一样的。

sentences.en: Now, they're specific in Kubernetes, horizontal and vertical pod autoscalers that you can put in to your cluster.
sentences.zh: 现在，在 Kubernetes 中它们是具体的，你可以将水平和垂直 Pod 自动扩缩容工具放入你的集群中。

sentences.en: And then you have a cluster autoscaler underneath all of that, which is actually managing the nodes.
sentences.zh: 然后在所有这一切的底层，你有一个集群自动扩缩容工具，它实际上在管理节点。

sentences.en: Because fundamentally, even if you have a vertical pod autoscaler that says, as this node becomes busy, you know, bump up the number of CPU cores it has, it might actually
sentences.zh: 因为从根本上说，即使你有一个垂直 Pod 自动扩缩容工具，它说当这个节点变忙时，你知道的，调高它拥有的 CPU 核心数，它实际上可能

sentences.en: physically run out of the CPU cores on the machine, the node that it's running on.
sentences.zh: 会物理上耗尽它所运行的那台机器（节点）上的 CPU 核心。

sentences.en: So it might need to add more nodes or make the node bigger.
sentences.zh: 所以它可能需要添加更多节点或者把节点变大。

sentences.en: So you have a cluster autoscaler actually underneath all of these that are very specific to the cloud provider and can add and remove nodes based on
sentences.zh: 因此，在所有这些的底层，你有一个集群自动扩缩容工具，它们非常特定于云提供商，并且可以根据

sentences.en: the aggregate demand in the cluster.
sentences.zh: 集群中的总体需求来添加和删除节点。

sentences.en: And then you have the horizontal pod autoscaler, which is just adding more containers, adding more pods as the load goes up.
sentences.zh: 然后你有水平 Pod 自动扩缩容工具，随着负载上升，它只是添加更多容器、添加更多 Pod。

sentences.en: And generally, the way to think about it is if you have a very parallelizable workload, like, you know,
sentences.zh: 通常，思考这个问题的方式是，如果你有一个高度可并行的工作负载，比如，你知道的，

sentences.en: serving web requests where a lot of this stuff can be done in parallel, it's great to use something
sentences.zh: 提供网页请求，其中很多事情可以并行完成，那么使用诸如

sentences.en: like a horizontal pod autoscaler and just have more replicas to load balance that load between.
sentences.zh: 水平 Pod 自动扩缩容工具并拥有更多副本来在它们之间分担负载是非常棒的。

sentences.en: If you have something that is very serial and cannot be parallelized easily, it might just be worth throwing, you know, a bigger node at it, something that say requires
sentences.zh: 如果你有一些非常串行且无法轻易并行化的工作负载，那么给它分配，你知道的，一个更大的节点可能更值得，比如某种需要

sentences.en: a ton of memory to compute and is, you know, has these big spikes like a machine learning workload
sentences.zh: 大量内存来计算且具有巨大峰值的东西，就像机器学习工作负载那样，

sentences.en: that you need to load all the data in, and then, you know, process it in some way all sitting on one node worth using the vertical pod autoscaler for that.
sentences.zh: 你需要将所有数据加载进来，然后，你知道的，以某种方式全部在一个节点上处理它，这种情况下使用垂直 Pod 自动扩缩容工具是值得的。

sentences.en: But again, these things don't operate in isolation, they're happening together with multiple applications on a single cluster.
sentences.zh: 但话又说回来，这些东西并不是孤立运行的，它们是在单个集群上与多个应用程序一起发生作用的。

sentences.en: And then the nodes under the hood need to actually react to it.
sentences.zh: 底层的节点实际上需要对此作出反应。

sentences.en: And that's why we have a cluster autoscaler as well.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么我们也有集群自动扩缩容工具的原因。

sentences.en: It's adding, removing and right sizing nodes.
sentences.zh: 它在添加、删除和调整节点大小。

sentences.en: And, you know, you have a lot of interesting projects that are coming out just in the last few years, like Carpenter from AWS,
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道的，在过去几年里涌现出许多有趣的项目，比如 AWS 的 Karpenter，

sentences.en: that's supposed to help solve this problem and make sure that you're getting the most optimal
sentences.zh: 它旨在帮助解决这个问题，并确保你能够从成本和性能的角度获得

sentences.en: nodes from both the cost and performance perspective added and removed from your EKS cluster based on the
sentences.zh: 最理想的节点，根据 HPA（水平 Pod 自动扩缩容工具）和 VPA（垂直 Pod 自动扩缩容工具）的

sentences.en: demand of the HPA horizontal pod autoscaler and the VPA, the vertical pod autoscaler.
sentences.zh: 需求，将其从 EKS 集群中添加或删除。

sentences.en: Cool.
sentences.zh: 酷。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So horizontal autoscaling seems like relatively simple.
sentences.zh: 所以水平自动扩缩容看起来相对简单。

sentences.en: Like imagine the way I would imagine it is you could look at, I guess, the delay in between the time a request arrives and when it
sentences.zh: 就像，我想象的方式是，你可以查看，我猜是请求到达的时间与它

sentences.en: can be processed by one of these nodes, and then just continue to add more nodes that that seems to,
sentences.zh: 能够被其中一个节点处理的时间之间的延迟，然后继续添加更多节点，这似乎，

sentences.en: it seems like I could understand how you could build a, like a Kalman filter or something to like, you know, or a PID controller or something to like the horizontal autoscaling.
sentences.zh: 这似乎让我可以理解你如何构建一个卡尔曼滤波或者某种东西来，你知道的，或者一个 PID 控制器之类的东西来进行水平自动扩缩容。

sentences.en: Vertical seems really difficult, right?
sentences.zh: 垂直扩缩容看起来非常困难，对吧？

sentences.en: Because you have to, it's like, if you run out of memory, it's almost too late at that point to say, oh, I need more memory.
sentences.zh: 因为你必须，这就好比，如果你内存耗尽了，到那个时候再说“哦，我需要更多内存”几乎已经太迟了。

sentences.en: Or, you know, it's like, you might be halfway through the process and say, oh, let me start the whole thing over again with twice as many CPUs.
sentences.zh: 或者，你知道的，这就好比，你可能已经进行到进程的一半，然后说：哦，让我用两倍的 CPU 从头重新开始整个过程。

sentences.en: But then you didn't really save anything because you already were halfway done.
sentences.zh: 但那样你其实什么也没省下来，因为你已经完成了一半。

sentences.en: So like, how does the vertical
sentences.zh: 所以，垂直

sentences.en: autoscaling actually work?
sentences.zh: 自动扩缩容究竟是如何运作的？

sentences.en: I mean, what sort of signals do you get back to actually do that?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，你究竟会得到什么样的信号反馈来实际做到这一点？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So, I mean, it, it actually is difficult.
sentences.zh: 所以，我的意思是，它确实很困难。

sentences.en: In fact, you know, one of the big production use cases we run internally is a lot of Argo workflows, which is another layer of orchestration on top of
sentences.zh: 事实上，你知道的，我们在内部运行的大型生产用例之一是大量的 Argo 工作流，这是 Kubernetes 之上的另一层编排，

sentences.en: Kubernetes for, you know, specific ETL workflows.
sentences.zh: 用于特定的 ETL 工作流。

sentences.en: And some customers will just send us a ton of data and we have to scale up sort of dynamically the pods based on that.
sentences.zh: 有些客户会直接发送大量数据给我们，我们必须根据这些数据动态扩展 Pod。

sentences.en: And it's difficult.
sentences.zh: 这很困难。

sentences.en: We got a lot of crash back off loops and things like that when, you know, the pod runs out of memory or can't initialize.
sentences.zh: 当 Pod 内存耗尽或无法初始化时，我们遇到了很多崩溃循环退避（crash back off loops）之类的问题。

sentences.en: So it's, you know, I will sitting here with the experience of having run this thing.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道的，我正带着运行这套系统的经验坐在这里。

sentences.en: It's not a solved problem.
sentences.zh: 这不是一个已经彻底解决的问题。

sentences.en: Like, I'll tell you that the easiest thing to do is over provision, essentially for the peak in advance.
sentences.zh: 比如，我会告诉你，最简单的事情就是过度配置，基本上是为了高峰期提前做好准备。

sentences.en: And VPA is great at scaling things down, I found, but not so great at scaling things up as you alluded to.
sentences.zh: 而且正如你所提到的，我发现VPA在缩减规模方面很棒，但在扩容方面却没那么出色。

sentences.en: And, you know, I have the scar tissue of a lot of failed clusters and, you know, data that didn't populate on a backfill to prove that it's not a solved problem.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，我有很多失败集群的“伤疤”，还有回填时未能填充的数据来证明这不是一个已经彻底解决的问题。

sentences.en: And, you know, it's hard to predict the future, especially when you have large spikes in your workload requirements.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，预测未来很难，特别是当你的工作负载需求出现大起大落的时候。

sentences.en: If you have something like an easy sort of scale up, that's very linear and predictable.
sentences.zh: 如果你遇到那种很容易扩容的情况，那是高度线性和可预测的。

sentences.en: That's different than, you know, spikes of data coming in at arbitrary points, which I don't think there's any system, you know, short of just over provisioning to really handle
sentences.zh: 这与那些在任意时间点涌入的数据峰值不同，我认为除了过度配置之外，没有哪个系统能真正处理

sentences.en: that effectively.
sentences.zh: 得那么高效。

sentences.en: Scaling down is a different story, right?
sentences.zh: 缩减规模则是另一回事了，对吧？

sentences.en: And great to save money.
sentences.zh: 而且这对于省钱非常有用。

sentences.en: But if that comes at the expense of performance for a critical customer, you know, it's a trade-off you as an engineer have to make.
sentences.zh: 但如果这是以牺牲关键客户的性能为代价的，你知道，这就是你作为一名工程师必须做出的权衡。

sentences.en: Yeah, that makes sense.
sentences.zh: 是的，这说得通。

sentences.en: I'm going to jump in here and interrupt our interview today to talk about our sponsor, Zencaster.
sentences.zh: 我要插话打断我们今天的采访，来聊聊我们的赞助商Zencaster。

sentences.zh: Zencaster是一个一体化的播客制作套件，无需所有这些专业技术知识，就能为你提供演播室品质的音频和视频。

sentences.en: It records each guest locally and uploads the crystal clear audio and video right into the suite.
sentences.zh: 它会在本地录制每个嘉宾的画面，并将清晰无比的音视频直接上传到套件中。

sentences.en: So you have high quality raw materials to work with.
sentences.zh: 这样你就有高质量的原始素材可以处理了。

sentences.zh: 我和杰森做Programming Throwdown节目已经有一段时间一直在使用Zencaster，相比我们以前的做法，这是一个巨大的升级。

sentences.en: It's so much easier and more seamless to have everybody join a Zencaster room and get individual
sentences.zh: 让每个人加入一个Zencaster房间，并为每个参与者获取独立的

sentences.zh: 音频流，要容易得多也顺畅得多，这使得剪辑和后期制作能够进行得快得多。

sentences.en: It just also feels like a better experience for all involved.
sentences.zh: 对于所有参与的人来说，这也感觉是一次更好的体验。

sentences.en: I'm so happy that we have this new solution instead of the way we used to do things back when we first started.
sentences.zh: 我很高兴我们有了这个新方案，而不是回到我们刚开始时那种老旧的做法。

sentences.zh: 如果你想尝试使用Zencaster来制作你自己的播客，你可以通过访问zen.ai斜杠programming throwdown来获得免费试用。

sentences.en: That's zen.ai slash programming throwdown.
sentences.zh: 也就是 zen.ai 斜杠 programming throwdown。

sentences.en: Back to the podcaSt.
sentences.zh: 回到播客。

sentences.en: Yeah, I remember it's a long time ago, but there was this machine learning job that I would run
sentences.zh: 是的，我记得那是很久以前的事了，当时我在一家不同的公司运行着一个机器学习任务

sentences.en: at a different company and we would always crash the first time because of the autoscaler.
sentences.zh: 由于自动扩缩容的原因，我们每次都会在第一次运行的时候崩溃。

sentences.en: So basically, sometimes you'd crash twice.
sentences.zh: 所以基本上，有时你得崩溃两次。

sentences.en: And so I think in the end, we ended up putting some kind of constraint saying, don't even bother starting this job unless you have 20 gigs of RAM or something like that.
sentences.zh: 所以我想最后，我们最终设置了某种限制，大意是：除非你有20G的内存或类似的东西，否则甚至都不要费心去启动这个任务。

sentences.en: And that comes to the other nice point of Kubernetes, which is when you're launching one of these pods, you can hard code what the memory and CPU requirements are.
sentences.zh: 这就谈到了Kubernetes的另一个好处，那就是当你启动其中一个Pod时，你可以把内存和CPU需求硬编码进去。

sentences.en: And the system, in theory, depending on how it's configured, will have to go and get those for you before you get the pod in.
sentences.zh: 理论上，系统会根据它的配置情况，在你获得Pod之前去把这些资源为你找来。

sentences.en: So that's generally how you, as a practitioner, as you were saying, get around those issues.
sentences.zh: 所以，作为实践者，正如你所说，这通常就是你绕过这些问题的方式。

sentences.en: You're not saying like, start this with an arbitrary amount and figure it out for me.
sentences.zh: 你不会说“用一个随意的量启动这个然后帮我想清楚”。

sentences.en: You can say like, give me this much, otherwise it won't work, which I think is the model that most folks,
